name: Alt-Lite
summary: A loose, mostly online and American right-wing current that emerged around 2016-2017 and defines itself against both mainstream conservatism and the white-nationalist alt-right. It combines Trump-aligned populism, cultural or civic nationalism, opposition to illegal immigration and often to Islam, hostility to feminism and political correctness, and a free-speech and anti-establishment stance. Its adherents deny ethnic or racial hierarchy, though critics dispute how sincere that is.
scope: The 2016-2018 'alt-lite' or 'new right' milieu named by the ADL: figures such as Milo Yiannopoulos, Mike Cernovich, Gavin McInnes (Proud Boys founder) and Paul Joseph Watson, using the Breitbart 2016 guide and their documented statements. It excludes the white-nationalist alt-right, mainstream conservatism and later violent Proud Boys splinters. There is no program, so most economic and institutional answers are low-confidence inferences, and members differ widely (libertarian vs economic-nationalist).

universal-healthcare.rationale: Cernovich floated single-payer while others in the milieu are market-minded; no shared line, so split.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Welfare-sceptical, Trump-aligned milieu is unlikely to push a large minimum-wage rise; inferred, not documented.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Cultural libertarians like Yiannopoulos lean market, but the economic-nationalist strand is mixed; inferred.

public-ownership.rationale: Nationalising industry is not an alt-lite theme and the movement is Trump-aligned and anti-socialist; inferred.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Not a concern of the movement; Republican-aligned adherents generally oppose higher taxes on the wealthy.

unions-good.rationale: Anti-left and pro-business Trumpism; no documented union support, so a weak inference.

property-fundamental.rationale: Cultural-libertarian strand values property rights, though not a defining theme.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Anti-big-tech censorship complaints coexist with deregulatory Trumpism; adherents are split.

cut-welfare.rationale: Wikipedia notes alt-lite members criticise welfare spending.

worker-ownership.rationale: Collective ownership is a left idea the movement opposes as anti-left; inferred.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Anti-establishment free-speech rhetoric and security-minded nationalism pull opposite ways.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Libertarian-leaning members favour it, while McInnes's Proud Boys tenets are anti-drug; genuinely split.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Opposing speech limits and political correctness is a defining theme; free-speech rallies were a hallmark.

strong-leader.rationale: Strongly pro-Trump populists, but explicit calls to bypass institutions are not documented; inferred.

state-harmful.rationale: Minimal-government rhetoric exists but nationalists want a strong state for borders; most reject abolition.

limit-guns.rationale: Gun rights are listed among Proud Boys tenets by press accounts and are standard for the Trump-aligned right.

empower-police-military.rationale: Law-and-order Trump right supports police and military; inferred from Trump alignment.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Libertarian-minded provocateurs may agree while socially conservative members disagree; split.

decide-locally.rationale: No documented stance; nationalists favour a strong national government but libertarians favour localism.

rehabilitation.rationale: Law-and-order Trump right favours punishment over rehabilitation; inferred.

traditional-family.rationale: McInnes's group venerates the housewife and opposes feminism, stressing traditional gender and family roles.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Split: Yiannopoulos opposed it in Australia, while gay figures within the milieu and many members accept it.

abortion-legal.rationale: Social-conservative leaning of the Trump right, though libertarian members dissent; inferred.

more-religion-public.rationale: Cultural-Christian defence of the West against Islam, but many members are secular provocateurs; split.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The Proud Boys refuse to apologise for Western civilisation and oppose racial guilt; the milieu rejects identity-based remedies.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Anti-feminist and anti-LGBT-rights movement rejecting social-justice gender theory.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Cultural nationalism is the defining alt-lite position, set against alt-right ethnic nationalism.

gradual-change.rationale: Anti-establishment disrupters, but not revolutionary; leaning against respect for established institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Opposes illegal immigration and many oppose Muslim immigration; less than the alt-right's call for sharp cuts overall.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Nationalist, anti-globalist Trump-aligned milieu rejects supranational authority.

free-trade.rationale: Cernovich calls himself an economic nationalist; Trump-aligned trade scepticism is common.

nation-first.rationale: Nationalism and Trump's America First are core to the movement.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The alt-lite is generally non-interventionist; Cernovich criticised the Syria strikes.

open-borders.rationale: Closed borders is a stated Proud Boys tenet and opposition to illegal immigration is central.

limit-growth.rationale: Pro-Western-progress culture warriors oppose degrowth; inferred.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Trump-aligned right opposes drastic climate regulation; not a central theme.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: No documented stance; optimism and tech-sceptic anti-big-tech views coexist.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Pro-growth Trump right tends to favour it; inferred.

revolution-justified.rationale: Rhetoric of violence against antifa exists but adherents don't claim revolution; inferred.

experts-over-public.rationale: Hostile to media, academia and establishment expertise; populist anti-elite stance.

central-planning.rationale: Strongly anti-left and anti-socialist; central planning is opposed.

socialized-markets.rationale: Public or worker ownership is a left idea the movement opposes; inferred.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not addressed; no basis for a side.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Republican-aligned adherents oppose estate taxes; inferred.

basic-income.rationale: Cernovich has backed some form of basic income while others oppose welfare; split.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Economic-nationalist Trump-aligned stance, as Cernovich describes himself.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Economic nationalists might agree, libertarians not; no documented line.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Anti-communist and capitalist-leaning; abolition of wages rejected.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Libertarian members may agree, but no shared stance; split.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-run bargaining bodies are alien to this milieu; inferred.

one-party-rule.rationale: Movement celebrates free speech and Trump-era elections; one-party rule is rejected.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Neoreactionary monarchism belongs to the alt-right intellectuals, not this wing; split.

democracy-best.rationale: Civic nationalists work within electoral politics and support Trump, unlike alt-right critics of democracy.

direct-votes.rationale: Populist leanings but no documented support for referendums.

workers-councils.rationale: Left-socialist form of rule the anti-left movement rejects.

right-to-secede.rationale: Not addressed; libertarians might favour it, nationalists don't.

natural-rulers.rationale: Alt-lite distances itself from the alt-right's hierarchical, anti-egalitarian intellectuals.

political-violence-never.rationale: Proud Boys treat violence against antifa as a core tenet and some figures joke about it, though others deny it.

war-builds-character.rationale: Non-interventionist stance makes glorifying war unlikely; inferred.

separate-church-state.rationale: Mixed secular provocateurs and cultural Christians; split.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Cultural defence of the West is not theocratic; many members secular.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Not a movement theme; nationalists want a strong state.

military-superiority.rationale: America First nationalism favours a strong military, though non-interventionist.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Alt-lite explicitly rejects the alt-right's ethnic nationalism for civic or cultural nationalism.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Marxist concept opposed by the anti-left movement.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The Breitbart guide praises 'natural conservatives' who prefer hierarchy and order over radical egalitarianism, and Wikipedia says many in the alt-lite oppose welfare.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Refuses to apologise for the West's creation of the modern world.

civilizational-union.rationale: Civilisational Western identity appeals, but nationalism and America First cut against political union.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Cultural libertarian strand; no explicit statement.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Free-speech and gun-rights advocacy leans on individual rights; inferred.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental philosophy is not a topic in the sources; no adherent line to infer.

limit-population.rationale: Natalist traditionalism leans against limits; inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Western chauvinism celebrates the modern world.

accelerate-technology.rationale: No source ties the movement to accelerationism; tech enthusiasm and anti-big-tech views both appear.

human-enhancement.rationale: Libertarian leanings versus traditionalism; Cernovich is self-improvement oriented but no policy line.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anti-elite populism distrusts technocratic delegation; inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: Cultural nostalgia present but provocateurs also want disruption; split.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Cernovich says the new right is not bound to conservatism; weak signal.

direct-action.rationale: Rallies and street fights alongside electoral work for Trump; split.

means-match-ends.rationale: Prefigurative politics is not discussed in any source on the milieu.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Left-radical idea opposed by the movement.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Socialist principle opposed by anti-left movement.

production-for-use.rationale: Socialist principle opposed by anti-left movement.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Marxist claim rejected by the anti-left movement.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; a right-wing, pro-Trump movement that opposes welfare clearly rejects Marxist-Leninist class dictatorship.

taxation-theft.rationale: Libertarian-leaning members agree; nationalist conservatives do not.

harm-principle.rationale: Cultural libertarians accept it but social conservatives do not.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Breitbart authors call themselves cultural libertarians and oppose group identity politics.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Not addressed; movement is electorally engaged.

state-as-business.rationale: Trump business-style governance appeals, but not a stated idea.

positive-liberty.rationale: Welfare-sceptical stance rejects material-means conception of freedom.

media-academia-power.rationale: Claims that media, academia and the establishment police speech is a central theme of the Breitbart guide.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Breitbart guide endorses human biodiversity as a legitimate debate, but alt-lite officially disavows racial hierarchy; split.

organic-representation.rationale: Not addressed; adherents work through parties.

total-state.rationale: Not discussed directly; the movement's free-speech activism and opposition to welfare and political correctness clearly imply rejecting total state direction.

national-rebirth.rationale: Trumpist Make America Great Again narrative of decline and renewal.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Feudal loyalty is alien to the movement.

bound-labor.rationale: Never discussed; serfdom is clearly alien to a modern American civic-nationalist movement.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Rejects postmodern social-justice epistemology and defends Western reason.

universal-morality.rationale: Western chauvinism asserts the West's superior values; inferred universality.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Pro-Israel stance common in Islam-critical wing, though not universal; inferred.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Diaspora return rights are not a documented concern of this American-centred milieu.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival is not documented as a concern of an English-speaking online movement.

school-vouchers.rationale: Republican-aligned adherents usually favour school choice; inferred.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Not addressed; Trump-aligned but no line.

rule-by-example.rationale: Rule by moral example is a Confucian idea; the movement's provocative style suggests mild disagreement.

national-self-determination.rationale: Civic nationalism endorses each nation governing itself.

force-without-un.rationale: Non-interventionist and nationalist rejection of UN authority pull in opposite directions.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Secular provocateurs and religious members split.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Welfare-critical and anti-illegal-immigration; benefits for citizens only follows.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Welfare criticism implies work conditions; inferred.

class-collaboration.rationale: Class cooperation is not discussed; populist anger at elites and pro-business leanings cancel out.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Defends Western heritage rather than discarding it.

dominated-front.rationale: Western chauvinism opposes such anti-Western fronts.

workers-nation.rationale: Organising the working class nationally is not documented for this milieu.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Proud Boys venerate the housewife but law-based roles are not advocated; split.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Wikipedia says the alt-lite regards itself as separate from the white nationalist alt-right, its former adherents calling themselves civic nationalists instead.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Cultural nationalism requires immigrants to adopt national culture.

elite-replacement.rationale: Great Replacement ideas circulate in parts of the milieu while the alt-lite mainstream disavows them; split.

proportional-representation.rationale: Not addressed; Trump-aligned US adherents favour the existing system.

national-mission.rationale: Non-interventionist, yet Western chauvinism asserts superiority; split.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Anti-feminist; Yiannopoulos calls feminism man-hating and disputes the pay gap.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The Breitbart guide says natural conservatives were abandoned by both sides of the political establishment, and Milo vowed to dedicate his life to 'the destruction of the Republican Party'.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenic policy is an alt-right fringe theme not adopted.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Libertarian-leaning members agree, nationalists want more state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Rejects white-identity politics; Cernovich said he did not realise alt-right was ethno-nationalist.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Civic nationalists distance from racial hierarchy, though critics dispute sincerity.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Opposes guilt narratives about Western settlement.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Civic nationalism favours equal law for all; inferred.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Hindu nationalist issue absent from alt-lite.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Religion in schools splits secular provocateurs from cultural Christians; no documented line.

trade-surplus.rationale: Economic nationalist outlook favours a trade surplus.

population-transfer.rationale: Disavows ethnic nationalism; inferred but Muslim-immigration restriction adherents differ.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Proud Boys say they do not start fights but treat violence as a tenet; not absolutist.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Western chauvinism celebrates competitive modern West; weak inference.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Free-speech stance opposes banning parties; inferred.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Republican freedom theory is not discussed in any source on the movement.

separated-powers.rationale: US-centred adherents accept constitutional checks; inferred.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Labour law is not a documented concern; no basis for a side.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Poverty's causes are not discussed in the sources; no inference possible.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Breitbart guide argues integrating distinct groups is unlikely and mass immigration erodes cohesion, though attributed to alt-right.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sortition is alien to an electorally engaged, Trump-supporting movement; inferred rejection.

party-controls-media.rationale: The Breitbart guide urges 'free speech in the face of the regressive Left's censorship sprees', and Milo says his real concerns are 'pop culture and free speech'.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Capping politicians' pay is not documented; mild populist sympathy is offset by pro-business leanings.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Binding party discipline is not documented; the movement is loosely organised and individualist.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Not discussed directly; Wikipedia cites cultural nationalism and non-interventionism, and Milo applied to join UKIP, which clearly implies opposing the EU.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Executive command powers are not discussed; US adherents accept the existing constitutional arrangement.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is not a topic for this largely secular, online milieu.

clerical-rule.rationale: Wikipedia describes Milo as a counter-jihadist who calls fear of Islam 'entirely rational', and lists Islam among the things many in the alt-lite oppose.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Term limits are not documented as an issue for the movement.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall elections are not documented; populist sympathy and no stated position leave it split.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Non-interventionist currents agree; Trump-aligned conservatives mostly keep alliances.

people-in-arms.rationale: Gun-rights supporters but not militia-abolition of armies.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Rural moral superiority is not a documented theme of this largely online, urban-linked milieu.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Divided-nation reunification is not relevant to an American-centred movement.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Hostile to academia and elite media; populist theme.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The ADL reports that McInnes founded the Proud Boys as 'Western chauvinists who refuse to apologise for creating the modern world', the members' oath.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Secular-leaning provocateurs; many members reject it.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Libertarian and free-speech leaning provocateurs oppose it.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Civic nationalism rejects ethnic descent as the basis.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Opposes special treatment for minorities, notably Muslims; inferred.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Post-colonial economic critique is not in the movement's sources; mild disagreement inferred from capitalist leanings.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Constitutional rewriting is not discussed; no documented stance.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: America First nationalism opposes foreign aid; inferred.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Not addressed; US adherents accept the Electoral College.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Monetary institutions are not documented concerns; libertarian and populist strands disagree.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial compromise is not a documented topic; pro-Israel and non-interventionist strands differ.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Not addressed; anti-communist but no view on this debate.

collective-defense.rationale: Non-interventionist doubts versus nationalist military pride; split.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: International-law questions on annexation are not covered by the sources.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Defends Western Christian heritage vs Islam; inferred.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Ceremonial heads of state are not discussed; US adherents favour a partisan president.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Secession is not discussed in the sources; nationalists and libertarians would differ.

region-keeps-system.rationale: One-country-two-systems arrangements are not discussed in any source on the movement.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Not discussed; a divine head of state is clearly alien to an American civic-nationalist, free-speech movement.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax structure is not documented; libertarian and populist strands differ.

space-expansion.rationale: Space policy is not documented as a concern for the movement.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical mixed-constitution theory is not discussed; no stance can be inferred.

leader-cult.rationale: Trump devotion is strong, but formal leader worship is not advocated.

equal-parenting.rationale: Men's rights and manosphere-linked milieu favours father-friendly custody; inferred.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Apostasy law is not discussed; Milo's attacks on 'mainstream Muslim culture' for mistreating women and gay people clearly imply opposing such religious penalties.

women-must-cover.rationale: Opposes Islamic dress mandates; Yiannopoulos attacks mainstream Muslim culture on women.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Rejects ethnic nationalism and supranational union.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Minority strategy of emigration versus local rights is not a topic for this movement.

ban-cartels.rationale: Antitrust is not documented; anti-big-tech sentiment pulls one way and pro-business views the other.

no-bailouts.rationale: Not addressed; populist anger at elites vs pro-business.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Majoritarian limits on courts are not documented; populists may agree while civic nationalists value constitutional limits.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Quotas are not discussed; Milo is a frequent critic of feminism who disputes the gender pay gap, which clearly implies opposing parity mandates.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Economic nationalism is trade-sceptical but not autarkic; colonies irrelevant.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Prefers national tariffs to international standards; inferred.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Hereditary titles are irrelevant to an American-centred movement.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Western chauvinism wants Western civilisation taught without apology.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Western superiority view but non-interventionist; split.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Opposes racial guilt and preferences; core anti-identity-politics view.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary reform is not discussed; no documented stance.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Imperial legacy influence is not a documented concern of an American-centred movement.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Libertarian members agree, civic nationalists want to be seen as non-racist; split.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Gun rights and free speech defended constitutionally.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred: civic nationalists focus on current law and borders, and the sources show no interest in treaty revision.

elective-rulers.rationale: Inferred: the movement is American and civic-nationalist, so it holds that rulers are elected rather than inherit.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred from a majoritarian, anti-establishment populism; no stance on minority vetoes is documented.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred from anti-establishment rhetoric and American constitutional tradition; documentation is thin.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Inferred: it accepts elected legislatures as the lawmaking authority in the American model, while attacking the establishment.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Inferred: no program exists, but mainstream Western culture holds animal suffering matters.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred: a mainstream conservative-leaning view accepting use of animals with humane limits.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Members split between libertarian self-reliance and nationalist populism, and no line is documented.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Inferred: members are heavily engaged in online political activism and see politics as a fight to win.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Inferred from its attacks on the mainstream media and political correctness as tools that keep people docile.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Inferred from its talk of a liberal cultural establishment shaping opinion beyond coercion; documentation is thin.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Inferred: members are broadly pro-capitalist or economic nationalists, not dependency theorists.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred: they deny ethnic hierarchy and stand for civic nationalism, so naturalized citizens are not second class.

party-own-road.rationale: The statement concerns socialist parties, which lie outside the milieu, and no line is documented.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Inferred from Trump-aligned America-First nationalism that is hostile to foreign aid.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Inferred: American civic nationalists have no irredentist claims and no stance is documented.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred from strong hostility to identity politics, which they say tries to rank groups by descent; the sources show no explicit line.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Inferred from hostility to Antifa and the left, while they deny being fascist and do not oppose anti-fascism as a value.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Inferred from strong anti-communism and opposition to authoritarians; their own denial of fascism makes this low.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Members are split and no line is documented in the sources.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from opposition to statue removal and political correctness; documentation is thin.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Anti-feminism and attention to men's issues are core to the current, per the cited sources on Yiannopoulos, Cernovich and McInnes.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Inferred from anti-feminism and attention to men's grievances; no specific statement is cited.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Inferred from defence of Western civilization and civic nationalism; the sources do not address it directly.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Inferred: they venerate the military but remain constitutionalists who see politics as civilian.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred from hostility to feminism and a traditional-family bent; no stance is documented.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred from the milieu's traditional-family and Western-chauvinist stance; no documented position on filial obligation.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Anti-feminist, pro-traditional-family stance suggests opposition to abolishing legal marriage; inferred.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Free-speech and anti-establishment stance favours transparency, but no documented position.

local-production.rationale: Economic nationalists favour domestic production; libertarians do not; no shared line.

informal-organisation.rationale: Informal online networks are common, but the milieu backed Trump and mainstream politics, so no clear case against parties; inferred.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Nationalist, sovereignty-minded stance suggests priority for national law; inferred.

religious-nation.rationale: Defines itself as civic or cultural nationalist rather than religious; positions on Islam are cultural, not a religious definition of the nation.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The milieu's Trump-aligned nationalism stresses sovereignty and America First, so ritual submission to a leading power is inferred as strongly rejected.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: The milieu has no programme on interregional finance; libertarian and nationalist strands split on subsidies between regions.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Members favour private property and oppose communism, but the statement's common-ownership clause is not their position; support is partial and inferred.

defeat-communism.rationale: The milieu is anti-communist in rhetoric, but a policy of defeating communism abroad clashes with its non-interventionist streak, so support is moderate and inferred.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The libertarian and market-minded wing favours private providers, while the economic nationalist wing is less clear; inferred from general market leanings.

religion-illusion.rationale: The milieu defends Western civilisation and Christianity as heritage, though Yiannopoulos and others are personally mixed; the material-conditions theory is not theirs.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Members are generally pro-market and pro-Western achievement, so a progressive historical role for capitalism is inferred, though economic nationalists are critical of globalism.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Anti-feminism is a recurring theme, with feminism seen as harmful, and the milieu rejects structural economic explanations of gender inequality.

socialized-care.rationale: The Proud Boys and others stress traditional family roles and oppose state-run domestic services; inferred from their anti-feminist, traditionalist outlook.

purge-loanwords.rationale: The milieu defends Western culture but has no documented language-purism programme and often mocks state micro-management; inferred.

treaties-binding.rationale: The milieu has no documented position on treaties with internal nations; sovereignty-minded and rule-of-law instincts pull in different directions.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The milieu is individualist and pro-market, so common-property communities are inferred as strongly rejected.

majority-settlement.rationale: The milieu denies ethnic hierarchy and has no programme for state-steered settlement; it is inferred as opposed to such social engineering.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Members are largely pro-market, but the economic nationalist wing talks of a break from globalist capitalism; inferred as a mild rejection.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Western chauvinism and nationalism suggest sympathy for historical claims, but the milieu has no stated doctrine on land claims; inferred.

holocaust-denial.rationale: The alt-lite defines itself against the alt-right and its Jewish conspiracy and race hierarchy; Holocaust denial is not part of its stated positions, so this is inferred.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Libertarian-leaning, with openly gay figures such as Yiannopoulos, it is not documented as favouring criminal penalties.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Its free-speech stance opposes suppressing opposition, though figures backed strong enforcement against opponents; inferred.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: A free-speech, anti-political-correctness current opposes blasphemy law; inferred.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Economic nationalists favour national interest but the milieu has no colonial program; inferred.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Hostile to Islam as a political force and not part of its doctrine; inferred.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Opposes sharia and religious rule; inferred.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Populist and anti-establishment, but built around online personalities and a Trump-aligned right rather than workplace or campus democracy; inferred.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Hostility to feminism and political correctness is central, and it rejects identity-based oppression frameworks.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Critical of gender identity politics, as with Yiannopoulos, but reluctant to attack legal protection; inferred.

assisted-dying.rationale: Libertarian strand favours personal choice; the sources do not document a stance, so this is inferred.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: It defines itself against mainstream conservatism and the alt-right, and claims to combine the best of each; inferred.

alienated-labor.rationale: Critique of capitalism as alienating is a left argument that this right-wing current opposes; inferred.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Opposition to Islam is a defining theme, with Yiannopoulos and McInnes attacking Islam and Muslim immigration.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Secular or civic-nationalist, with a free-speech outlook; inferred.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Anti-Islam views suggest support for restricting religious dress such as the hijab in state institutions; inferred.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Libertarian lean and no stated stance on employment law; inferred.

social-market-economy.rationale: Libertarian and economic-nationalist strands split, but neither endorses a social-market compromise; inferred.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Nationalist and pro-Trump, it favours strong defence; inferred.

rich-first.rationale: Pro-business Trump alignment favours growth and enterprise over redistribution; inferred.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Trump-aligned America First stance leans against entanglements, though Cernovich notes interventionism; inferred.

missingStatements.text: Western civilisation is superior to other cultures and its achievements should not be apologised for.
missingStatements.rationale: The Proud Boys' founding creed is 'Western chauvinism', refusing to apologise for creating the modern world.

missingStatements.text: Feminism has harmed men and society more than it has helped.
missingStatements.rationale: Anti-feminism is a recurring theme: Yiannopoulos calls feminism man-hating and the Proud Boys oppose it.

missingStatements.text: Muslim immigration to Western countries should be stopped.
missingStatements.rationale: Yiannopoulos opposes Muslim immigration and calls fear of Islam rational, though the alt-lite as a whole is less uniform.

notes: Contested label: some named figures reject it, and critics (Media Matters, ADL) argue it blurs into the alt-right. Libertarian and economic-nationalist strands answer economics differently, so many answers are low confidence.
